audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Trundle five of seven stages in a lane Malphite wins 56.12% over 547 games, and it contradicts the entry's own prose: whys[4] says 'the lane flips to me', whys[5] calls first item 'my power peak', whys[6] says 'I out-frontline him'. All three sit under stages the chart hands to Trundle.
audit.why: Levels 3-5 really are his — Chomp is a flat 3.5s at 300 range with an attack reset, and King's Tribute heals him off every minion that dies near him, so he sustains through anything a pre-Thunderclap Malphite does. But 56% is one of Malphite's better lanes and the swing at 6 is real.
audit.corrected: Trundle owns Levels 1-3 through Level 5. From Level 6 onward the stages are Malphite's, matching both the 56.12% headline and the entry's own reasoning.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3] and late say 'never solo-fight him with R down' and treat Subjugate as an occasional threat window, with no cooldown attached to either ultimate.
audit.why: The numbers invert the advice. Subjugate is 120/100/80s; Unstoppable Force is 130/115/100s. His ultimate is back before yours at every single rank, and the gap widens as they rank — 80s against 100s at rank 3. 'Fight him when your R is up' therefore describes a window that mostly does not exist in the side lane. It also steals Health, Armor AND Magic Resist, doubling the amount stolen over four seconds, which is a direct tax on the stat Ground Slam's damage is calculated from.
audit.corrected: Subjugate 120/100/80s against Unstoppable Force's 130/115/100s — his ultimate is up first at every rank. It takes Health, Armor and MR and doubles the theft over 4s, hitting both your defence and Ground Slam's damage at once.
sources: champ-data/_kits/malphite.json (R cd 130/115/100; E scales with Armor)

audit.whatIsWrong: King's Tribute is never mentioned, and Frozen Domain appears only as a 'move-speed field'. There is no anti-heal advice anywhere in the content layer, although the full layer's win condition is literally 'Anti-heal and poke, don't duel'.
audit.why: King's Tribute heals Trundle a percentage of the maximum health of any unit that dies near him — in a lane, that is every minion in the wave, which is why he out-sustains a Malphite who is only trading chip. Frozen Domain then increases healing from all sources while he stands on it. Those two together are the sustain the entry keeps describing without naming, and Grievous Wounds is the answer to both. The two layers currently disagree: full says anti-heal is the win condition, content never mentions it.
audit.corrected: King's Tribute heals him off every minion that dies near him, and Frozen Domain (18s at rank 1) amplifies all his healing while he stands on it. Grievous Wounds is core, not situational.
sources: champ-data/_kits/trundle.json (P King's Tribute; W Frozen Domain, cd 18/17/16/15/14)

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet-flagged as having no cooldown sequencing anywhere, and it does not: Chomp is 'his Q bite', Pillar of Ice is 'his E pillar', Frozen Domain is 'his W move-speed field', with no numbers on any of them.
audit.why: The cooldowns are what make the advice actionable and they point in different directions. Chomp is a flat 3.5s at 300 range with an attack reset — you cannot wait it out, so the only answer is not being at 300. Pillar of Ice is his longest at 21s at rank 1, so the 21 seconds after a pillar is the walk-up window. Frozen Domain is 18s. Telling a player to 'bait his cooldowns' without those three numbers gives him nothing to act on.
audit.corrected: Chomp flat 3.5s at 300 range — unwaitable, so hold spacing instead. Pillar of Ice 21s at rank 1 is his longest cooldown and your walk-up window. Frozen Domain 18s at rank 1.
sources: champ-data/_kits/trundle.json (Q cd 3.5 range 300; E cd 21/19.5/18/16.5/15 range 1000; W cd 18/17/16/15/14)

audit.why: The entry's central claim — that Chomp's attack-damage steal is nearly worthless against Malphite — checks out and is worth keeping. Chomp saps Attack Damage; Thunderclap's aftershocks and Ground Slam both scale off Malphite's Armor and AP, not AD. It is the one place this entry is ahead of the others in the champion's file.
sources: champ-data/_kits/trundle.json (Q: 'sapping some of their Attack Damage')

edits.before: Trundle owns the opening stages and I just have to absorb it. His Q bite steals my attack damage every trade, so I make no progress autoing him and he out-sustains anything I throw — at levels 1-3 I have no trade pattern anyway, so I farm on Granite Shield and refuse to brawl. Do not stand in his W move-speed field trying to contest CS; he'll kite around me and bite again. The one good thing: his Q steal is wasted effort the more I lean tank, and he has no burst to punish a passive Malphite, so eating a little poke costs me nothing.
edits.after: Trundle owns the opening and you just absorb it. Chomp is a flat 3.5s at 300 range with an attack reset, so it is not a cooldown you wait out — it is a range you stay out of. King's Tribute heals him off every minion that dies near him, which is why nothing you chip in sticks, and Frozen Domain amplifies all of that healing while he stands on it, so do not contest CS inside it. Farm on Granite Shield resets and refuse to brawl. The consolation: Chomp steals attack damage, and a tank Malphite has none worth taking.

edits.before: Level 6 is where I take the lane back. Unstoppable Force is the one thing Trundle's kit cannot answer — he has no dash, no stun, no untargetability to cancel a committed R, so my knock-up lands clean and starts my all-in or a jungle collapse. Before that, levels 4-5, I stabilize as W (Thunderclap) and E (Ground Slam) come online: my E attack-speed slow blunts his auto-reliant Q-empowered bites, and the armor from W starts turning my autos into AoE splash he can't out-trade. Watch for his E pillar trying to wall me mid-engage — angle my R so a pillar can't body-block the dash.
edits.after: Level 6 is where you take the lane back. Unstoppable Force is the one thing Trundle's kit cannot answer — no dash, no stun, no untargetability — so the knock-up lands clean and starts your all-in or a jungle collapse. Before that, at 4-5, you stabilise as Thunderclap (W) and Ground Slam (E) come online: Ground Slam is a flat 7s and its attack-speed cut blunts the auto-reset bites Chomp rides on. Pillar of Ice is his longest cooldown at 21s and it is impassable terrain, so angle your R where a fresh pillar cannot sit between you and him.

edits.before: From first item on I'm favoured and it only widens — stacking armor (Bramble Vest into Sunfire) makes my W splash and E magic damage scale up hard, while his signature Q AD-steal does almost nothing to a tank with no AD to take. His one real answer is Subjugate (R): it steals a chunk of my armor and MR, and since my E and W damage scale off armor, that's the exact stat he's gutting. So I never duel him 1v1 with my R down — I respect his Subjugate window and instead bring my R to teamfights, where one Unstoppable Force into his squishies wins the fight regardless of how much sustain he has.
edits.after: From first item on you are favoured. Armour here is an offensive purchase — Ground Slam's damage is calculated from it — while Chomp steals attack damage a tank does not have. His answer is Subjugate, which takes Health, Armor and MR and doubles the theft across four seconds, gutting your defence and Ground Slam's damage in one cast. Do not plan around out-waiting it: at 120/100/80s it is up before your 130/115/100 ultimate at every rank. Buy Grievous Wounds against King's Tribute and Frozen Domain, and bring your R to fights rather than the 1v1.

notes: Packet defect confirmed: this entry had no cooldown numbers anywhere. Added the three that change decisions — Chomp is a flat 3.5s at 300 range, which is not a cooldown you wait out but a range you stay out of; Pillar of Ice is his longest at 21s at rank 1 and is therefore the walk-up window; Frozen Domain 18s. BIGGEST CORRECTION: the entry's rule was 'never solo-fight him with R down', which implies a window where yours is up and his is not. Subjugate is 120/100/80s and Unstoppable Force is 130/115/100s — his ultimate is back first at every rank, and the gap grows to 80s against 100s. Also added King's Tribute and Grievous Wounds: the content layer described his sustain repeatedly without naming the passive that produces it or the item that answers it, while the full layer's stated win condition is 'Anti-heal and poke, don't duel'. UNVERIFIED, LEFT ALONE: mid says to angle R so a pillar cannot body-block the dash. Riot's text says Pillar of Ice becomes impassable terrain but says nothing about interrupting a dash already in flight, so I kept the existing wording and did not strengthen it. VOICE: this entry is written in the first person ('I', 'my') throughout, unlike the rest of the champion file. The strings I rewrote are now in the site's second person; the ones I did not touch are still first person and need a pass.
